block-guide:
CORE/POST-CONTENT (Content) Draws the current page's or post's own blocks. Two places only: - A Fabrement template's content slot: the alternative to fabrement/content-source. Exactly one of the two per template. It shows page content only; it cannot select a theme PHP file. - Inside a Query's post-template: each listed post's full content. Placed in a page's own content it draws nothing (WordPress stops it repeating the page).
MARKUP (attributes only; no HTML of its own) <!-- wp:post-content {"align":"full","layout":{"type":"constrained"}} /--> As an entry: {"name":"core/post-content","attributes":{"align":"full","layout":{"type":"constrained"}}}. Drawn as <div class="entry-content wp-block-post-content ...">.
WIDTH layout "constrained": paragraphs keep the theme's content width, and alignfull / alignwide sections of the page still reach the screen / wide width. layout "default": nothing is limited. Unlike content-source it takes align ("wide", "full"): with align "full" it may sit in a constrained group and still span the screen. In a template without a layout attribute the template's contentWidth decides ("full" = default, "constrained" = constrained).
PITFALLS - A Fabrement template replaces the whole page: the frame must place its own header and footer (core/block refs) and the title if wanted (core/post-title). The page body is not a place for them. - Prefer fabrement/content-source in a new template: it does the same and can later take theme file rules without changing the frame.
CHECK Open a page assigned to the template: its content appears once, at the slot.
